| 501-fable | RL at the eval depth only: fine-tune and sample at 8 loops, never shallower | claude-fable-5-1 | rl, sampling, loops, schedule | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 31 | 629 | 493 | 1076 | discard | 0.958 | 0.0878 | 677 923 1035 1093 1127 | 3036 | 629 at 8 loops (665/612/609) against 675: fine-tuning and sampling only at the eval depth lost 46. The 2-loop diagnostic collapsed to 493 (502/473/504; per-sample dev accuracy 0.27-0.31 against 0.40-0.46 at 8 loops), so metric minus diag is +136, but only because 2 loops stopped being trained: at 8 loops itself per-sample dev accuracy was 0.40-0.46 against 500's 0.48 on seed 0. The fixed depth did not help the depth it was trained at. RL at 8 loops found proofs fast: after one round of 12 attempts, seeds 0 and 1 had solved 677 and 637 targets (500: 287 after 32 attempts over 1/2/4/8); seed 2 started at 208 (round-1 variance, as in the spike) and reached 1054 by round 5. RL-target accuracy at 8 loops ended at 0.66-0.72 (500: 0.76) and final solved 1127/1047/1054 (500: 1198). A round cost 335-380 s (the fine-tune at 8 loops 160-215 s against about 110 s at random 1-8; sampling 160-190 s charged), so seed 1 got 4 rounds. Fewer attempts and rounds explain part of the loss, but not the lower per-sample accuracy at the trained depth: the random 1-8 draw in fine-tuning acts as a regularizer (stochastic depth), not as the suppressor of deep passes I hypothesized. Pretraining was unchanged and again depth-invariant (val loss within 0.002 across 1-8 loops on every seed). Next: keep random depths in the fine-tune and change something else (deep supervision, a loop-count signal, or more attempts at deep loops only). |
| 502-claude | RL retries only the targets 1 loop failed, each at 2, 4 or 8 loops chosen at random | claude-opus-5-5 | rl, sampling, loops, schedule | 0.55 | 5400/300/1800 | 47 | 690 | 672 | 1203 | keep | 0.9565 | 0.0857 | 481 540 612 686 814 843 876 912 962 980 1001 1026 1057 1073 1087 1102 1119 1127 1140 1151 1160 1164 1170 1171 1172 1175 1182 1192 | 3934 | 690 at 8 loops (seeds 687/715/669) against 675 (698/686/641): +15, about one standard error of the difference between two 3-seed means, so kept by the rule, not shown beyond noise. As predicted, 7/7/6 RL rounds fit instead of 5/5/4 and RL solved 1203 targets against 1149. The eval gap did not move: 672 at 2 loops, so 8 loops add +18 (23/19/13), the same as 500. This improves RL; it does not make loops pay more at eval. The surprise is the randomized retries. I predicted depth would stop mattering on resistant targets after round 2; it did not. Of the targets that failed 8 tries at 1 loop, pooled over seeds and rounds (about 4,100 per arm, 24 tries each), 11.4% got a proof at 2 loops, 13.8% at 4 and 15.9% at 8 (per-sample acceptance 2.3%, 3.6%, 4.7%). In rounds 3+ it is still 10.4%, 11.7%, 14.3%, and 8 loops beat 2 in every seed (67 vs 57, 99 vs 58, 121 vs 95 targets), unlike the spike's flat curve on never-solved targets. Two caveats: the retry set is selected on failing at 1 loop, which favours loop counts least like 1 loop, and an 8-loop sample costs about 2x a 2-loop one, so per GPU-second 2 loops still cracks more. Round-1 yield depends heavily on the pretrained model (1-loop acceptance 0.159/0.038/0.052 by seed). |
| 503-fable | RL fine-tune trains each proof only at loop counts at or above the depth that found it | claude-fable-5-1 | rl, loops, loss, schedule | 0.4 | 5400/300/1800 | 54 | 663 | 630 | 1112 | discard | 0.931 | 0.0891 | 118 218 262 282 539 589 647 694 884 958 1000 1024 1053 1070 1097 1112 1124 1137 1146 1157 | 3101 | 663 at 8 loops (698/653/639) against 675: training each proof only at loop counts >= its discovery depth did not raise the deep computation, it only lowered the shallow one. The mechanism check went as predicted on the shallow side and failed on the deep side. Last-round RL accuracy at 1 loop fell from 500's 0.708/0.691/0.612 to 0.652/0.560/0.585 and the 1-vs-8 gap roughly doubled (0.048 to 0.092 mean, predicted >= 0.10), but accuracy at 8 loops did not rise: 0.733/0.664/0.675 against 500's 0.763/0.734/0.659, and the 4-vs-8 plateau is untouched (0.731 vs 0.733, 0.657 vs 0.664, 0.673 vs 0.675; 500: 0.763 vs 0.763). Eval told the same story: metric minus diag widened from +18 to +33 (28/35/38, predicted >= 35), entirely from the 2-loop diag falling to 630 (670/618/601, 500: 684/667/621), while per-sample dev accuracy at 8 loops was 0.473/0.438/0.420 against 500's 0.481/0.473/0.416. So the one-pass constraint was not what capped depth: freeing the core from reproducing deep-found proofs at 1 loop did not let 8 loops do more than 4, which is the spike's plateau again. Depth-8-only records were 12-17% of RL records in round 1 and 3-5% later; depth-1 records grew from 32-46% to 73-78% as the fine-tuned model re-found proofs shallow, so the curriculum thinned out by itself. Cost of the rule: the weaker shallow model found fewer proofs in the cheap 1-loop calls (seed 0 round 2: 539 targets at 1 loop against 500's 691), cumulative RL solved fell to 1112 (1157/1083/1097) from 1149, and seed 1 lost its 5th round by the 1.15x margin (370 s left, 348 s rounds), which explains most of its -33. Pretraining unchanged (val 0.089/0.085/0.084). Next: the shared core at 4 and 8 loops computes the same thing whatever the fine-tune asks; a depth signal (iteration embedding) or a pretraining loop distribution that rarely demands shallow depth would test whether the core can learn a non-converged iteration at all. |
| 504-claude | Truncated backprop through the loops: only the last 2 passes get gradient, earlier passes hand over a no-grad draft state | claude-opus-5-5 | loops, loss, rl | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 24 | 662 | 670 | 1209 | discard | 0.9615 | 0.0898 | 306 403 506 613 863 887 930 978 1028 1051 1071 1086 1100 1108 1119 1133 1138 1143 1148 1159 1167 1171 1176 1185 1190 1194 1197 1200 1204 1205 1208 1209 1211 1216 1221 1223 | 3526 | 662 at 8 loops (seeds 662/674/651) against 690: -28, and below the 2-loop diagnostic on every seed (676/682/652, mean 670), so metric minus diag went from 502's +18 (23/19/13) to -8 (-14/-8/-1). The pre-registered falsifier fired: after RL, 8 loops no longer beat 2. Per-sample dev accuracy 0.433/0.404/0.402 at 8 loops against 0.427/0.417/0.403 at 2 (502: 0.466/0.489/0.460 against 0.435/0.461/0.436). The 2-loop theorem count is unchanged (670 against 672) though its per-sample accuracy is lower, so in theorems the whole loss is the depth benefit. The throughput half of the prediction held and bought nothing: 4,858/4,780/4,774 pretraining steps (1.40x, as benchmarked) left val loss at 2 loops at 0.0898/0.0830/0.0852 (mean 0.0860 against 0.0866; predicted at or below 0.085), and 9/9/8 RL rounds against 7/7/6 solved 1,209 targets against 1,203. At equal round count the fine-tuned model was behind: 1-loop accuracy on RL targets 0.696/0.681 after 6 fine-tunes on seeds 0/1 against 0.73/0.74, and 0.677 against 0.731 after 5 on seed 2. The retry comparison shows where depth went. On the pretrained model deeper retries still helped (round-1 per-sample acceptance at 2/4/8 loops 0.045/0.069/0.089, 0.049/0.078/0.077, 0.014/0.020/0.026 by seed) and pretraining val loss at 8 loops was at or below 2 loops on every seed, so truncation did not break deep passes in pretraining. After fine-tuning the advantage was gone: pooled over seeds and rounds, resistant targets were cracked 11.4% at 2 loops, 12.7% at 4 and 12.6% at 8 (502: 11.4/13.8/15.9), and in rounds 3+ 9.2/9.6/9.3 (502: 10.4/11.7/14.3). Interpretation, not established: the premise that passes before the last two carry no useful gradient is wrong. With truncation the first core pass, which does most of the work (1 loop reaches 0.72 on RL targets), is differentiated only at loop counts 1 and 2, a quarter of the batches, so each step teaches the shared core less; and the +18 that 8 loops buy in 500 and 502 looks like something full backprop through the unrolled passes builds on the long RL proofs. Next: if throughput is wanted, narrow the loop range with full backprop (the spike's 1-4 arm) instead of cutting the gradient; if depth is wanted, the lever is more end-to-end gradient through deep unrolls on hard proofs, not less. |
| 505-fable | Countdown embedding: every pass of the shared core is told how many passes remain before its state is decoded | claude-fable-5-1 | architecture, loops | 0.45 | 5400/300/1800 | 56 | 681 | 662 | 1181 | discard | 0.958 | 0.0791 | 424 493 582 676 861 889 931 962 1011 1020 1044 1067 1087 1094 1109 1124 1131 1136 1147 1159 1163 1172 1177 1183 1185 1186 1187 1191 | 3451 | 681 at 8 loops (678/710/655) against 502's 690 (687/715/669): -9, inside noise, discard. This is the 'signal ignored' branch of the preregistration, with one nuance. The countdown rows were learned but stayed small: after RL their norms were 0.41-0.93 against an entry-output norm of 20 (2-5%; the pre-registered 'used' threshold was 25%, 'ignored' below 5%), largest for rows 3-6 (passes far from the end) and smallest for rows 0-1. The iteration still converges fast: the relative change of the core state per pass at 8 loops after RL was 0.28, 0.10, 0.046, 0.025, 0.017, 0.016 and then 0.022-0.027 on the last pass. That final uptick is the one visible use of the countdown, on every seed (0.012 to 0.020 after pretraining, 0.016 to 0.027 after RL): the countdown-0 pass does a small distinct 'finalize' step while passes 4-7 sit near a fixed point. The loop gap did not move: metric minus diag +19 (17/22/18; 502: +18, 500: +18). Per-sample dev accuracy at 8 vs 2 loops 0.470/0.489/0.435 vs 0.437/0.457/0.406, a gap of 0.033 against about 0.02 on 502 seed 0, but the 8-loop accuracy itself is not above 502's 0.48. The surprise is pretraining: val loss at 2 loops 0.079/0.082/0.076 (mean 0.079 against 502's 0.087), the lowest of this loop so far, with a small depth dependence appearing on two seeds (1 loop 0.0836 vs 0.0820 at 8 on seed 1, 0.0805 vs 0.0758 on seed 2, seed 0 flat within 0.0001), and none of it carried to RL or eval. The 1-loop program got slightly weaker, which 502's 1-loop-first schedule pays for: round-1 one-loop acceptance 0.137/0.024/0.044 (502: 0.159/0.038/0.052), cumulative RL solved 1181 (1191/1192/1160 vs 1203). RL rounds 7/6/6 (502: 7/7/6); seeds 1 and 2 each missed a 7th round by the 15% margin (232 s and 238 s left against about 245 s needed). Steps 3460/3408/3469, 6,403,328 params, no speed change, no crash. Interpretation: letting the core know how many passes remain is necessary but not sufficient for a non-converged iteration; with the same next-token loss at every depth, gradient descent keeps the converged one-pass-plus-refinement program and uses the budget signal only to adjust the final pass. Next: a loss that only deep passes can lower (depth-dependent targets, or a loop distribution without n = 1 combined with the countdown so intermediate states are never decoded), or spend the spare 3.6M parameters, since 502's model is at least as parameter-limited as depth-limited. |
| 506-claude | Untied first pass: pass 1 of the loop gets its own two blocks, the shared core only refines (9.56M parameters, same compute per loop count) | claude-opus-5-5 | architecture, loops | 0.5 | 5400/300/1800 | 23 | 665 | 654 | 1174 | discard | 0.9425 | 0.0811 | 147 206 268 317 706 766 820 874 919 953 989 1023 1047 1059 1073 1096 1113 1122 1133 1140 1148 1152 1160 1167 | 3309 | 665 at 8 loops (seeds 652/688/655) against 690 (687/715/669): -25, below 502 on every seed (-35/-27/-14). Both pre-registered effects failed. Capacity: six unique blocks at 2 loops scored 654 (635/675/653) against the tied trunk's 672, per-sample dev accuracy 0.388/0.408/0.408 against 0.435/0.461/0.435 (predicted at least 680 and 0.45), although pretraining did fit better as predicted (val loss at 2 loops 0.0811/0.0814/0.0857, mean 0.0827 against 0.0866; 3,355/3,378/3,377 steps). Refinement: metric minus diag was +11 (17/13/2) against 502's +18 (predicted at least +25; seed 2's +2 is no gain), and per-sample dev accuracy rose from 2 to 8 loops by 0.024/0.038/0.027, mean 0.030, against 502's 0.028 (predicted at least 0.04). A shared core that only ever refines buys the same +0.03 per sample from six more applications as a core that also does the first pass, so the dual role is not what limits depth. The retry arm of the falsifier fired: targets that failed 8 tries at 1 loop were cracked 21.9% of the time at 2 loops, 23.6% at 4 and 23.9% at 8, pooled (1.09x from 2 to 8; 502: 11.4/13.8/15.9, 1.39x), and on seed 0 8 loops cracked fewer than 2 (250 against 276 of 1,394). The gap arm stopped just short (+10.7 against a threshold of +10). The loop is not vestigial, but the step that matters is now 1 loop to 2, the shared core's first application: the 2-loop crack rate is nearly double 502's because the 1-loop model is much weaker, and that is where the run was lost. After 5 fine-tunes, 1-loop per-sample accuracy on RL targets was 0.583/0.588/0.592 against 502's 0.715/0.718/0.731 at the same round (predicted 0.69-0.75), though pretraining left the 1-loop path as good as 502's (val loss at 1 loop 0.0840/0.0819/0.0921 against 0.0859/0.0825/0.0950; 1 loop minus 2 loops +0.0029/+0.0005/+0.0064, mean +0.0032, the bottom of the predicted range). More targets failed the cheap pass (402/382/397 in round 6 against 343/335/333), rounds after the first averaged 263 s against 241 s, and seeds 0 and 1 lost their 7th round with 176 s and 100 s left (6/6/6 rounds, predicted 7/7/6). The retries made up for the weak first pass in discovery: cumulative RL solved after 6 rounds was 1,167/1,188/1,166 against 502's 1,171/1,191/1,196 at round 6 (final 1,174 against 1,203). The lost round does not explain the result: on seed 2, where both runs had 6 rounds, this is still -14 at 8 loops, and per-sample dev accuracy at 8 loops is lower on every seed (0.412/0.446/0.435 against 0.466/0.489/0.460). Interpretation, not established: in the tied trunk every batch at any depth trains the weights that the 1-loop pass runs and is decoded from, which is why 1 loop stays within about 0.05 of 8 loops on RL targets there (500); untied, the first-pass blocks are decoded directly in 1 fine-tune batch in 8 and otherwise learn to feed the core, and each untied block gets one application's gradient per step of a 600-step fine-tune. Weight tying is doing useful work for RL, and 3.16M more parameters with a better pretraining loss gave a fine-tuned model that is worse on dev at both depths, so parameters are not the bottleneck under this budget. Next: keep the first pass tied. The gain from 2 to 8 loops has been +0.02 to +0.03 per sample in 500, 502 and here, whatever the core was asked to do, which points away from the core's role and toward what the training data demands of depth. |
